resources.string:
This app turns your earphones into a personal sound amplifier. It is not a medical hearing aid and does not replace a hearing professional.

• Start with the volume low and raise it slowly.
• Loud sound for long periods can damage hearing.
• See a doctor about sudden hearing loss, ear pain, dizziness or ringing.
• For profound deafness, use the Captions tab.
Lowers steady noise like fans, traffic, engines and hum
Tip: put the phone near the person talking (on the table, or let them hold it) to hear them clearly over room noise.
Not a medical device. Start with low volume. If you have sudden hearing loss, pain or ringing, see a doctor.
Earphones disconnected. Sound is paused so the phone speaker doesn\'t howl.
Connect wired or Bluetooth earphones to start.
Bluetooth adds about 0.15–0.3 s of delay, so voices may not match lips. Wired earphones give the most natural sound.
Connect earphones first. Using the phone speaker would cause loud feedback.
About 5 minutes. You\'ll hear short beeps at different pitches, one ear at a time. Tap the big button every time you hear a beep, even if it is very faint.
• Sit somewhere quiet.\n• Wear the earphones you will use with the app (left and right the right way round).\n• The app sets the volume itself during the test.
Your hearing aid has been tuned to this result. Fine-tune it in the Adjust tab.
Lower on the chart = you need louder sound at that pitch.
Speech around you appears here as text. Hearing aid sound pauses while captions are on.
No speech recognition service on this phone. Install or enable Google speech services.
Microphone permission is needed for captions.
No internet. Download an offline speech pack for your language in phone settings.
Your phone\'s speech service doesn\'t support this language. Choose another, or install it in phone settings.
Raise a pitch if voices sound muffled or unclear; lower it if it sounds sharp or tinny. Changes apply instantly while the hearing aid is on.
Uses the phone\'s built-in voice-call processing. Can help in noise; sounds less natural.
Turns the hearing aid on by itself when earphones are connected.
While it is on, the notification has Quieter, Louder and Turn off buttons, even on the lock screen.
Swipe down from the top twice, tap the pencil and drag the Hearing aid tile in. Tap it to switch on or off from anywhere.
Some phones close background apps to save battery. Set this app to “Unrestricted” or “Not optimized”.
Battery saving won\'t stop this app.
Turns your earphones into a personal hearing aid, with a hearing test and live captions.
Free for personal, non-commercial and educational use. Commercial use needs a license.
Downloaded and checked. If Android asks, allow installs from this app, then tap Install.
Couldn\'t reach GitHub. Check your connection and try again.
The download didn\'t pass its safety check, so it wasn\'t installed. Try again later.
This release has no Android app file yet.
Connect your earphones, tap START and listen. Begin with low volume and raise it slowly. The notification lets you change the volume or turn it off from anywhere.
In a quiet room, wear your earphones and tap the big button every time you hear a beep, even a faint one. The app then tunes each ear and each pitch for you. You can take it again any time.
Wired earphones sound the most natural. Bluetooth earphones such as AirPods or Galaxy Buds work too, but add a short delay, so voices may not match lips.
Choose a situation (Conversation, Noisy place, TV & music) and keep “Reduce background noise” on. In a loud room, put the phone near the person speaking.
A whistle means sound leaks from the earphones back into the microphone. Lower the volume, push the earphones in further, or keep the phone away from your head.
For profound hearing loss, Captions shows speech as large text. Choose the language people around you speak. Some phones need internet or an offline speech pack.
The hearing aid keeps working with the screen off. Use the notification buttons, or add the Quick Settings tile to switch it on and off. See More › Background & shortcuts.
This app is not a medical device. Loud sound can harm hearing. See a doctor about sudden hearing loss, ear pain, dizziness or ringing. Only use it to listen where you are allowed to.
